import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1188

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1188](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1188)
-/

namespace Erdos1188

open Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- A congruence class `(n, a)` represents `a (mod n)`. -/
abbrev CongruenceClass := ℕ × ℕ

/-- The modulus is `> 1` and the residue is reduced. -/
def ValidClass (c : CongruenceClass) : Prop := 2 ≤ c.1 ∧ c.2 < c.1

/-- `z` lies in the class `(n, a)`. -/
def Satisfies (z : ℤ) (c : CongruenceClass) : Prop := z % (c.1 : ℤ) = (c.2 : ℤ)

/-- Every integer satisfies some congruence of `S`. -/
def Covers (S : Finset CongruenceClass) : Prop := ∀ z : ℤ, ∃ c ∈ S, Satisfies z c

/-- No two classes of `S` share a modulus. -/
def HasDistinctModuli (S : Finset CongruenceClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃c₁⦄, c₁ ∈ S → ∀ ⦃c₂⦄, c₂ ∈ S → c₁.1 = c₂.1 → c₁ = c₂

/-- A minimal distinct covering system: valid classes with distinct moduli that
cover `ℤ`, with no proper subset already covering. -/
def IsMinimalDistinctCoveringSystem (S : Finset CongruenceClass) : Prop :=
  (∀ c ∈ S, ValidClass c) ∧ HasDistinctModuli S ∧ Covers S ∧
    ∀ T : Finset CongruenceClass, T ⊂ S → ¬ Covers T

/-- All classes `(n, a)` with `2 ≤ n ≤ x` and `a < n`. -/
def ClassesUpTo (x : ℕ) : Finset CongruenceClass :=
  (Finset.Icc 2 x).biUnion fun n => (Finset.range n).image fun a => (n, a)

open scoped Classical in
/-- `F(x)`: the number of minimal distinct covering systems all of whose moduli
lie in `[1, x]`. -/
noncomputable def coveringCount (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((ClassesUpTo x).powerset.filter IsMinimalDistinctCoveringSystem).card

/--
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ with associated congruence
classes $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ a distinct covering system if every integer satisfies at
least one of these congruences. A minimal distinct covering system is one such
that no proper subset forms a covering system. Let $F(x)$ count the number of
minimal distinct covering systems with all moduli in $[1,x]$. Estimate $F(x)$.

The estimate is `log(log F(x)) / log x → 1`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-1188/Research/SparseAsymptotic.lean"]
theorem erdos_1188 :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => Real.log (Real.log (coveringCount x : ℝ)) / Real.log (x : ℝ))
      atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1188

status_issues.source_status: As retrieved on 2026-09-07, erdosproblems.com still marks #1188 OPEN. Its separate proof-claims page records a full proof claim by Colin Snyder, submitted 2026-07-15, for exactly F(x) = exp(x^(1+o(1))), but does not record an accepted resolution.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1188 says “OPEN” and “This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.” https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1188/proof-claims lists the July 15 claim and cautions that appearing there does not mean anyone associated with the site has examined the proof.
status_issues.suggested_change: Reconcile the source's official OPEN status with the verified Lean result, potentially by updating the source rather than downgrading this theorem. The formal_proof attribute is supported by the kernel check and should not be removed on this evidence. If the source retains OPEN for a sharper estimation problem, distinguish that broader question from this solved exponent-scale result.

reformulations.difference: The source describes congruence classes with increasingly ordered distinct moduli; Lean counts finite sets of canonical pairs (modulus, least nonnegative residue).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every congruence class modulo n > 1 has exactly one representative with 0 ≤ a < n. Distinct moduli give a unique increasing ordering of the resulting pairs, so the encoding neither multiplies the count by permutations nor identifies different systems. Covering and deletion of subfamilies are preserved. The lower bound 2 in ClassesUpTo agrees with the source's explicit 1 < n₁. Membership in the counted finite set and the equivalence of Satisfies with integer congruence on valid classes were verified in Lean; the full representation bijection was checked mathematically.

reformulations.difference: The proposed estimate in the source's proof-claim entry is F(x) = exp(x^(1+o(1))); the declaration uses the double-logarithmic limit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On a tail where F(x) > 1 and x > 1, set e(x) = log(log F(x))/log x − 1. Then F(x) = exp(x^(1+e(x))) exactly, and the stated limit is equivalent to e(x) → 0. Conversely, taking logarithms of that representation gives the ratio 1+e(x). In scratch.lean I proved this equivalence and independently proved F(x) ≥ 2 for every x ≥ 12 using two explicit minimal covering systems. Thus Mathlib's logarithm and division defaults at small inputs cannot alter the equivalence.

review.notes: All nine declarations were checked; no mathematical defects were found. Scratch checks prove coveringCount 0 = coveringCount 1 = coveringCount 2 = 0, inclusion-minimality facts, and coveringCount x ≥ 2 for x ≥ 12. The exact pinned external proof's 31-module dependency closure was concatenated in import order and checked under Lean 4.33.1 with backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency set to false for compatibility with its Lean 4.31 source; no mathematical declarations were changed. Its counting function equals this file's definitionally, and both the external theorem and the bridge to the repository statement have only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] as axioms. Hence the status discrepancy is not evidence of an invalid formal proof. The website's April 17 discussion explicitly acknowledges that its counting question differs from the disjoint-modulus packing question in Er80 p.95; this file faithfully follows the question currently posed by its cited website. Certificates are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/external_combined.lean.
